The Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates to the Second Continental Congress [d2][d7]. John Hancock, as President of the Continental Congress, was the first to sign the engrossed copy on August 2, 1776, using a large, bold signature [d4][d7][d9]. The other delegates signed by geographic order, from the northernmost state (New Hampshire) to the southernmost (Georgia), and notable signers included Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Edward Rutledge (the youngest signer at age 26), and Benjamin Franklin (the oldest at age 70) [d4][d6]. Not all delegates were present on August 2nd; late signers included Elbridge Gerry, Oliver Wolcott, Lewis Morris, Thomas McKean (identified as the last to sign), and Matthew Thornton, while some delegates such as Robert R. Livingston never signed at all [d7][d8].
